content.title: Timothée Chalamet Gives Standing Ovation for Misty Copeland After Her Rousing Sinners Performance at 2026 Oscars
content.text: 0 seconds of 25 secondsVolume 0% NEED TO KNOW Misty Copeland and Shaboozey performed “I Lied To You” from Sinners at the 98th Academy Awards, along with Miles Caton and Raphael SaadiqCopeland’s appearance followed her response to Timothée Chalamet’s controversial comments on ballet and operaPEOPLE can confirm that Chalamet, nominated for Best Actor for Marty Supreme, gave the performance a standing ovation from the audience Sinners officially came to life on the Oscars stage! At the 98th Academy Awards on Sunday, March 15, some of the stars of the film — the most nominated movie in Oscars history — took the stage at the Dolby Theatre to perform “I Lied To You,” with some help from Misty Copeland and Shaboozey. The famed ballerina, 43, and the country star, 30, lent their talents to the show-stopping rendition, along with Miles Caton and Raphael Saadiq, who collaborated on the track for the 2025 horror-action movie. Saadiq opened the performance on guitar before Caton joined with vocals, alongside support from Shaboozey. Shaboozey performing at the 2026 Oscars. Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times via Getty During the performance, the audience was transported into a recreated “Pierce the Veil” sequence from the film, where dancers representing generations of musical influence gathered inside a 1930s Mississippi juke joint. Alabama Shakes frontwoman Brittany Howard added vocals to the performance, as Sinners star Jack O'Connell was spotted dancing in the audience. The performance concluded with Copeland’s powerful ballet moves taking center stage. Misty Copeland performing at the 2026 Oscars. Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times via Getty PEOPLE can confirm that Timothée Chalamet nominated for Best Actor for Marty Supreme, gave the performance a standing ovation from the audience. This comes after his comments about opera and ballet caused backlash within the arts community. Copeland’s appearance on the Academy Awards stage comes a week after the ballerina made headlines for weighing in on the backlash surrounding nominee Timothée Chalamet after he slammed both ballet and opera during his Variety and CNN town hall with Matthew McConaughey. Timothee Chalamet at the 2026 Oscars; Misty Copeland performing at the 2026 Oscars. Kevin Mazur/Getty; Rob Latour/Shutterstock After the Oscar-nominated Marty Supreme actor, 30, said during the Feb. 24 town hall that "no one cares about" the art forms, the professional ballet dancer addressed his comments while speaking on a panel in New York City on Sunday, March 8. "First I have to say that it's very interesting that he invited me to be a part of promoting Marty Supreme with respect to my art form," Copeland said, adding, "I think that it's important that we acknowledge that, yes, this is an art form that's not 'popular' and a part of pop culture as movies are. But that doesn't mean it doesn't have enduring relevance in culture." Copeland — who made history in 2015 as the first Black woman promoted to principal dancer at the American Ballet Theatre — also said that Chalamet “wouldn't be an actor and have the opportunities he has as a movie star if it weren't for opera and ballet in their relevance in that medium.” The ballerina's appearance also comes after she shared an Instagram post in early March revealing she had undergone hip surgery and was prioritizing her recovery, writing that she was focused on “healing — physically, mentally, and patiently.” Miles Caton in 'Sinners' (2025). Courtesy Warner Bros via Capital Pictures Ahead of the Oscars, the show’s executive producer and showrunner, Raj Kapoor, and executive producer Katy Mullan said that they wanted the Sinners performance to pay “homage to the film’s singular visual style.” The special tribute performance of “I Lied To You” — which was nominated for Best Original Song at the awards show — also featured the talents of Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone “Kingfish” Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush and Alice Smith. Related Stories The “I Lied To You” rendition featuring the talents of Copeland, Shaboozey, Caton and Saadiq was one of two film-dedicated performances to grace the Oscars stage on Sunday. The other — as announced ahead of the ceremony — highlighted KPop Demon Hunters. The Best Animated Feature Film nominee, which is Netflix’s most-watched film of all time, was honored on the Oscars stage with a “fusion of traditional Korean instrumentalists and dance,” executive producers Kapoor and Mullana said ahead of the ceremony. Misty Copeland in 2023. The voices behind the animated blockbuster’s band HUNTR/X, Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami, took the stage for the film’s track “Golden,” which also received a Best Original Song nod.
